title: Anchor and tide rollout notebook (personal)
body:
Goal: quick personal reference for an "anchor + tide" style release I want to try for model flips where we keep a small stable anchor cohort and gradually float traffic (tide) across other cohorts. Informal, half-baked — use caution.

Brief idea:
- Anchor cohort: 2–3% of traffic pinned to the previous stable model variant for at least 48h. Serves as baseline for regressions.
- Tide cohorts: sequential cohorts (A/B/C) that get stepped up through 5%, 15%, 40%, then full traffic. Each step is a short plateau to validate metrics.
- Siphon buckets: small shadow-only cohorts used to prime caches and detect silent regressions (no user-visible traffic, only telemetry).

Why this?
- Keeps a durable baseline (anchor) long enough to compare drift in latency/errors/quality.
- Tide pattern helps reduce sudden capacity shocks and makes cost spikes easier to diagnose.

Immediate checklist (for next flip):
- [ ] Create release branch and tag (git tag rflip/<model>-<date>)
- [ ] Upload model to registry and note digest (keep immutable tag)
- [ ] Build deployment manifest with explicit version pinning for anchor and tide cohorts
- [ ] Add canary route in routing policy: anchor=2%, tideA=5%->15%->40%->100% (steps defined), siphon=0.5% shadow-only
- [ ] Add rollout TTL for each step and automated rollback thresholds
- [ ] Add pre-provision warmup job (priming hot KV for popular prefixes)
- [ ] Notify #deploys + oncall an hour before soft-open

Operational runbook (quick):
- Warmup: run priming script with representative prompt set (top 200 prefixes) for 30 mins before any traffic shift. Command: ./tools/prime_kv.sh --model <tag> --duration 30m
- Monitor:
  - Latency P50/P95 (goal: within 10% of anchor),
  - Error rate (4xx/5xx) and RPC failures,
  - Token cost-per-request (to catch unexpected token expansion),
  - Quality signal: regen-rate and top-1 BLEU-ish proxy from eval hooks,
  - Business metric: percentage of client retries and chat-abandonment in the last 10m.
- Abort conditions (anyone can trigger):
  - P95 latency increases > 35% vs anchor for 5m,
  - Error rate doubles baseline and absolute > 0.5%,
  - Regen-rate (client-side fallback) > 1.5% absolute increase,
  - Observed hallucination spike on eval set (manual check).
- Quick rollback: flip routing back to anchor (command: rcli route set --policy anchored --anchor-only) and open incident channel.

Metrics tagging plan:
- Tag rollout metrics with: rollout_id, model_digest, cohort, step_number, warmup_state.
- Ensure trace correlation id is propagated to evaluation hooks (so we can tie a bad sample back to cohort).

Priming and cache considerations:
- Danger: naive priming may overfit KV to synthetic prefixes. Use live-sampled prefixes from the last 6h (top 1k) and shuffle.
- Sequence length variation: prime both short and long sequences. Long sequences can expose slow paths.
- For quantized variants, run priming at lower concurrency to avoid hitting kernel warmup issues.

SDK / client-facing toggles:
- Use client-side header X-RINF-ROLLSET to mark cohort in requests for debug logs.
- Have SDK expose soft-flip flag so we can rapidly shift clients during a hotfix window.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Does a 2% anchor captured baseline cover enough signal for low-volume endpoints? probably not — might need per-tenant anchors for high-variance customers.
- Siphon buckets: how often do silent regressions appear in shadow vs live traffic? hypothesis: shadow reveals subtle logits drift faster. Need to test.
- Does priming reduce P95 regressions on first-traffic jumps? likely yes, need A/B with no-priming.

Timeline sketch (for a single region flip):
- T-4h: build and tag, smoke tests on staging
- T-2h: upload model, run priming (30m), create cohort routes but keep at 0%
- T: announce start, open anchor 2% -> observe 30m
- T+1h: open tideA to 5% -> hold 45m monitor
- T+3h: tideA to 15% -> hold 1h monitor
- T+6h: tideB to 40% -> hold 2h monitor
- T+9h: full shift, deprecate anchor after 48h stable

Fallback options:
- Instant rollback to anchor cohort (routing flip)
- Capacity fallback: shift traffic to cheaper model variant if latency threshold breached (auto-policy)
- Client pinning: provide per-tenant pin request endpoint for critical customers (manual opt-out)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep model digest immutable in the route (no live swaps). Rolling model binary must be separate deployment.
- Watch GPU mem fragmentation at high tide steps (especially on quantized 4-bit builds).
- Add discrete eval checkpoints in console for anchor vs tide cohorts so product team can flag quality fast.

Quick sketch of rollout_id naming: rflip-<modelname>-<date>-tide-<incremental-seed>

Example quick commands: (notes, not final)
- Tag: git tag -a rflip/llama-v2-20251103 -m "rflip llm v2"
- Push: git push origin rflip/llama-v2-20251103
- Route set: rcli route create --id rflip-llama-20251103 --policy anchor_tide --anchor 2% --tide-config "5,15,40" --siphon 0.5%
- Prime: ./tools/prime_kv.sh --model rflip/llama-v2-20251103 --prefix-file top1k.txt --concurrency 4 --duration 30m

Stuff to copy into a nicer doc later:
- Decision matrix for anchor size (2% vs 5% vs per-tenant)
- Rollout automation policy template (thresholds, step-duration, auto-rollback)
- Priming job knobs (concurrency, prefix sample window, sequence length mix)

Random brain dump ends here. Will tidy into a proper PRD if we decide to run this pattern more broadly.

-- Priya

(Notes: informal. If you see something wrong ping me. This is my working scratchpad.)
